title: Two triple fits with equal inner stars predict the HD 303514 eclipse signal in 1,502 plates excluded from fitting
abstract: We fit a Newtonian triple state to 1,490 strict DASCH APASS plates of HD 303514 and 44 published modern timing and shape constraints. We assume equal inner stars with a total mass of four solar masses. Two local fits link the binary blue and V light fractions and limit added light to the same or a redder color. Gaussian and Student-t plate errors give an outer period near 593 days, a tertiary-to-pair mass ratio near 0.50, mutual inclination 5.3-5.5 degrees and binary light fraction near 0.70. In 1,502 broader-cut plates excluded from the orbit fit, the predicted signals give squared-loss gains of 21.82 and 21.26. None of 1,999 tested wrong-phase shifts is larger. This is a conditional within-survey control, not a global false-alarm probability. Residual shape tests do not show a strong APASS mismatch; the ATLAS calibration has marginal tension. Both linked-color states retain both eclipses through 2060, with the primary minimum near 2031 at 48-52 percent of modeled early-2026 depth. A fourth star is not required to construct these tested fits. Limits include local searches, inherited modern shape constraints, plate calibration and color assumptions, shared survey errors and no radial velocities or calibrated orbit confidence region. Source observations remain external. Code, input hashes, fitted states and aggregate tests permit reproduction.
